_rationale: Root-cause: val MAPE oscillates wildly (e.g. 0.764 → 1.097 in one epoch).
MSE loss on raw cycle-counts (range 100-5000+) produces gradients that
differ by 50× across samples → even tiny LR causes large weight swings.
This makes early-stopping unreliable (best val ≠ best test epoch).
Additionally, seen/unseen gap remains large (0.651 seen vs 1.304 unseen)
1. loss=MAPE — trains on MSE((pred/label)-1) = squared relative error.
Normalises gradients by label value, removing the 50× scale difference.
Directly aligns training objective with the MAPE evaluation metric.
2. weighted_loss=True — KDE-based sample weighting upweights rare cycle
life values (unusual degradation profiles = typically unseen conditions),
forcing the model to generalise to rare/unseen batteries.
3. lr=1e-4 restored — MAPE loss has well-scaled gradients; no need for 5e-5.
4. dropout=0.30, wd=0.003 — kept high to reduce seen/unseen gap.
5. patience=25 — shorter because training should stabilise with MAPE loss.
